description: This dataset series gives structured risk assessment indicators for flood and drought at administrative level 2, produced by the Heidelberg Institute for Geoinformation Technology with its GAIA processing pipeline and published per country on the Humanitarian Data Exchange; the Kenya dataset is the example read. Indicators are derived from open sources such as WorldPop population, OpenStreetMap facilities and roads, and Google Earth Engine layers, on the common operational administrative boundaries. Tables cover access to services such as travel time to health facilities, counts of facilities, coping capacity, demographics, rural population, the rural accessibility index, vulnerability, evacuability and flood exposure. The Kenya files are dated February to August 2026 and are refreshed about every six months. Files are free CSV downloads under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike licence. Caveats: indicators inherit the completeness of OpenStreetMap, district aggregates hide local variation, and methods may change between releases. Simulation uses: ranking districts by access to healthcare and evacuation capacity for flood and drought scenarios, weighting emergency response demand, and validating accessibility models. Related records: Global maps of travel time to hospitals (data-global-travel-time-emergency-tertiary-hospitals) give a worldwide access layer and healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) supplies facility points.
